text:
Research supports separating product relationships from compatibility evidence. The [TREC 2025 recommendation guidelines](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html) distinguish functional substitutes, conceptual substitutes, full complements, complements with unknown compatibility, and incompatible complements. This directly supports reporting missing evidence separately from demonstrated mismatch. For diagnostics, require explicit conflicting model numbers, connectors, formats, or dimensions before declaring incompatibility. Treat substitute similarity as potential redundancy; interaction timestamps establish sequence and recency, but cannot establish ownership, satisfied needs, or whether another purchase is unwanted.

Text-based attribute extraction is feasible but requires local verification. [Brinkmann et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02130) study extraction and normalization from titles/descriptions, reporting 91% extraction F1 on WDC-PAVE; that result does not establish accuracy on these four Amazon categories. A practical probe should retain source spans, normalize units and identifiers, and return unknown for unsupported attributes. Audit a small category-stratified sample covering extracted values, missing values, and claimed conflicts; report precision, recall, evidence coverage, and pairwise relationship accuracy separately. These are proposed diagnostics, not measured results.

Selective prediction provides a framework for withholding unsupported diagnostic judgments. [Traub et al. (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/047c84ec50bd8ea29349b996fc64af4b-Paper-Conference.pdf) identify shortcomings in common aggregate metrics and propose AUGRC for undetected-failure risk. Applied here, report diagnostic error versus coverage on audited examples, including unknown rates per category. Keep these evidence-quality measures separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10 used for model selection.
